note: Simulated classically with the Python standard library — no quantum hardware. The lab proves the algorithms and benchmarks them against the classical methods, so the system is ready the day hardware can run them at scale. A simulated result is never a speedup claim.

grover.verdict: Found 1 in 16 in 3 steps with 96.1% probability; checking one by one takes 8 on average. Square-root speedup, not magic — and only once hardware exists.

qaoa.verdict: QAOA (simulated, p=1) expects a cut of 5.63 against greedy 8 and optimal 8. On this graph the classical method wins — p=1 is a shallow circuit. Deeper circuits and real hardware are what would pull ahead; the lab says so plainly instead of pretending otherwise.

vqc.verdict: VQC (simulated) scores 100% against the classical perceptron at 100% on the same toy data. The quantum classifier works — it ties the classical one at this scale and does not beat it. That is the honest result.
